focus: Two levels: full interlocking mark and rear-fin icon

studies.name: Shared edge
studies.brief: Stay very close to the selected tessellated-fin symbol. Refine the two long curved fin shapes and their shared ivory cut so that a small lowercase f is half concealed in the centre. Preserve the tilted compact diamond silhouette and heel holes. Secondary is the upper-left/rear fin alone, maintaining its exact orientation and outline from the primary.
studies.note: Closest to the selected idea. The shared edge hides the f until you look again.
studies.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand. Asset type: paired logo-system experimentation board for Finfolk, strictly freediving and freediving training. Input image 1 is the SELECTED tessellated-fins concept; develop this concept specifically, do not return to other logo directions. The user especially likes how one fin occludes a small lowercase f. Explore a TWO-LEVEL icon system: PRIMARY full interlocking two-fin symbol, SECONDARY only the rear/background fin extracted from the SAME primary. These are related levels of one mark, not two unrelated icons.
Composition: a clean square 1024x1024 identity board on warm ivory #eee5d3. Upper two-thirds: large primary full symbol on the LEFT; large rear-fin-only secondary icon on the RIGHT. Match their optical size. The rear shape in the right icon must have exactly the same contour, orientation, heel hole and internal cuts as the rear shape in the left icon. No arbitrary added bubble or dot. Both are flat midnight navy #172440 silhouettes with ivory negative space. Under them, one small centered readable lowercase serif wordmark "finfolk". Bottom row: show the same icon PAIR together in three restrained samples: navy on ivory, ivory on navy, cobalt and hot pink on acid yellow. In the two-colour sample, make the full icon's foreground fin cobalt and rear fin pink, and the secondary pink, so the layer relationship is absolutely clear. No text except "finfolk". No arrows, measurements, labels, photography, gradients, 3D, shadows, mockups, animals, divers, fish, spears, decorative pattern or watermarks. Minimal graphic precision and high-fashion optical balance.
Variation: Stay very close to the selected tessellated-fin symbol. Refine the two long curved fin shapes and their shared ivory cut so that a small lowercase f is half concealed in the centre. Preserve the tilted compact diamond silhouette and heel holes. Secondary is the upper-left/rear fin alone, maintaining its exact orientation and outline from the primary.

studies.name: The f revealed
studies.brief: Make the rear fin carry a clearer small lowercase f in its negative space. In the primary, the lower-right foreground fin intentionally overlaps and conceals about a third of that f, creating the quiet optical discovery the user liked. In the secondary, remove the foreground fin so the rear fin and its complete f can be seen. Keep the rear fin exactly the same geometry and position, simply reveal the occluded section.
studies.note: The primary conceals part of the f; the secondary reveals it in the rear fin.

studies.name: Long line
studies.brief: A more slender and elegant variation of the selected interlocking pair: elongate the freediving fin blades slightly, reduce internal cuts, and preserve the small f hidden at the shared edge. Primary is two tapered fin forms in a compact diagonal relationship, secondary is exactly the rear/upper-left fin removed from that same primary, with no redraw. Sophisticated, minimal and suited to small UI use.
studies.note: A quieter, slender version with fewer internal cuts for small interface icons.
